## Natural history notes

A small wave moth characterized by pale grayish to violet-tinged wings with fine wavy crosslines and delicate speckling, giving it a soft, washed appearance when resting. In Florida, it is found in warm wooded or semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, forest edges, parks, yards, and shrubby areas where suitable host plants and resting cover occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars likely feed on low plants or leaf litter, contributing to the broader food web as prey for spiders, birds, bats, and parasitoid wasps.
